answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance leverages game-theoretic auditing through topological cut verifications. Agents route trust across graph paths; any narrow inlet bridging isolated agent clusters is treated as a cut and audited by randomized peer validators. If a cluster attempts to harbor fake identities that emit a suspicious plume of coordinated claims, validators slash their bonded stake. Fabricating valid trust cuts scales with superlinear attacker cost relative to swarm size.
